description: Executor-level VelesQL conformance: asserts result ROWS / COUNTS / ORDERING, not just that a query parses. Golden ids are derived from velesdb-core (the source of truth); other executors (WASM, CLI) must reproduce the same result set for the same dataset+query. Shared read-only dataset; ordering is on unique payload fields so results are deterministic. `cases` must pass; `known_bugs` carry the expected result for a former core bug that is now FIXED — the regression-lock test (test_velesql_executor_known_bugs) runs un-ignored and must keep passing. Since v2.0.0 (issue #1544) the fixture also carries `extra_collections` + `join_cases` (JOIN ON/USING, core+WASM only — the CLI harness is intentionally untouched, see below), `aggregate_cases` (GROUP BY/HAVING via `execute_aggregate`, core+WASM only), `setops_cases` (UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, core+WASM only, membership/count only — see `documented_divergences` D003 for why ordering is NOT asserted), `match_cases` (1-2 hop MATCH, core+WASM only, per-executor query text — see D004 for why), and `documented_divergences` (informational: known, accepted core/WASM behavioural gaps, not pass/fail cases). `cases`/`dataset`/`known_bugs` are byte-for-byte compatible with v1.0.0 so the existing CLI conformance suite (which only reads those three keys) keeps running unmodified against the original 10 cases plus the new scalar-expression cases X011-X014, which use the same single-collection `docs` dataset and are safe for CLI's strict-order comparison. v2.1.0 adds LIKE/ILIKE/OFFSET (X015-X020) and NEAR under OR, alone and inside an AND (X021-X022), to `cases`, so the CLI runs them too, and, core+WASM only, the statement families the WASM executor implements on its own: `query_params` (the vectors every case below may bind), `near_cases` (NEAR ranking, hybrid NEAR + metadata, similarity() thresholds; ids in order plus `expect_scores`, compared within 1e-5), `fusion_cases` (NEAR_FUSED rrf/average/maximum and a trailing USING FUSION), `rejected_cases` (queries both engines must refuse), `dml_cases` (UPDATE/DELETE `statements` run on a fresh copy of the dataset, then `query` is asserted) and `projection_cases` (DISTINCT and named-column projection, compared as projected JSON rows). Also core+WASM only: `vector_group_cases` run a vector GROUP BY (NEAR + GROUP BY) and compare the order of its groups by `group_column`, and every `rejected_cases` entry names the `expected_code` both engines must refuse it with. v2.6.0 adds the `nums` extra collection and `number_cases` (plain SELECT, core+WASM, ids in order): numbers compare by exact value, `-0.0` equal to `0`, `0.3` not `0.30000000000000004`, an integer past 2^53 not the float it rounds to, an IN list the same at any length; core also runs them through a secondary index and the payload mirror. It adds G022-G025 (GROUP BY, MIN/MAX and HAVING over those numbers) and P006-P007 (DISTINCT `id`, PARTITION BY a number), and runs `projection_cases` over the extra collections too. v2.5.0 adds the `tickets` extra collection, whose payloads carry an `id` of their own, with O003 and G021 (`id` is the point id in WHERE, ORDER BY and aggregates). v2.4.0 adds G016-G020 (FIRST and tie order independent of scan order, `score` as a SQL GROUP BY alias, HAVING precedence) and R014-R015 (V018). v2.3.0 adds `null_order_cases` (plain SELECT over the extra collections, ids in order) and runs `aggregate_cases` over the extra collections too, pinning where a NULL sort key lands. v2.2.0 adds the Euclidean `docs_l2` extra collection and the `e` query vector for vector GROUP BY cases, which may also pin each group's row (`expect_rows`), id (`expect_ids`) and score (`expect_scores`, within 1e-5).

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: string equality filter + ORDER BY column ASC

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE year >= 2021 ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: integer range filter + ordering

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year DESC
cases.note: full scan + ORDER BY column DESC (no LIMIT)

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' AND year >= 2022 ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: conjunctive (AND) filter

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'other' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: filter selecting the complementary partition

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY category ASC, year DESC
cases.note: multi-column ORDER BY, mixed directions: 'other' (o<t) before 'tech', year descending within each group

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY category DESC, year ASC
cases.note: multi-column ORDER BY, opposite directions (category DESC, year ASC) — exercises independent per-column direction handling

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY category ASC
cases.note: tie-break lock: rows sharing the ORDER BY key are ordered by ascending point id (matches the index-backed ordered_ids walk, EPIC-081 phase 2)

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY category ASC, year DESC LIMIT 3
cases.note: EPIC-081 bounded top-k over a multi-column ORDER BY: bounded result equals the unbounded sort (X006) truncated to k

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC LIMIT 3
cases.note: EPIC-081 bounded top-k, ASC direction (complements the DESC regression-lock B001): full year-ASC order [5,1,3,2,4] truncated to k=3

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2022 ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: issue #1544: BETWEEN range-expression evaluation in WHERE

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE (category = 'tech' AND year >= 2022) OR category = 'other' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: issue #1544: parenthesized boolean expression evaluation, AND nested inside OR

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE NOT (category = 'tech') ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: issue #1544: NOT expression evaluation over a parenthesized predicate

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE year IN (2020, 2023) ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: issue #1544: IN-list expression evaluation

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category LIKE 'te%' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: LIKE with a trailing % wildcard

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category LIKE '_th%' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: LIKE with a single-character _ wildcard before a literal infix

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category ILIKE 'TE%' ORDER BY year ASC
cases.note: ILIKE matches case-insensitively

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
cases.note: OFFSET is applied after ORDER BY and before LIMIT: full year-ASC order [5,1,3,2,4], skip 1, take 2

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC OFFSET 3
cases.note: OFFSET without LIMIT keeps the rest of the ordered rows

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC LIMIT 2 OFFSET 10
cases.note: OFFSET past the end returns no row rather than an error

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR [0.8, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1] OR category = 'other' LIMIT 5
cases.note: NEAR under OR: the NEAR leaf is TRUE in a boolean context, so the disjunction admits every row and the NEAR ranking orders them (cosine to the query vector ranks all five rows apart). Core used to route this shape to the similarity() union executor, which dropped every NEAR hit and returned only the metadata side [3, 5], each scored 1.0

cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE (vector NEAR [0.8, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1] OR category = 'other') AND year >= 2021 LIMIT 5
cases.note: NEAR under OR inside an AND: with the NEAR leaf read as TRUE the WHERE reduces to year >= 2021, which filters the NEAR ranking

known_bugs.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE year >= 2019 ORDER BY year DESC LIMIT 2
known_bugs.note: REGRESSION LOCK (fixed): scalar ORDER BY <column> + LIMIT previously applied the LIMIT before the sort on the bounded top-k path (returned [2,1] instead of [4,2]); the bounded path now equals the unbounded path truncated to k, per KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md #9. expect_ids is the correct, currently-asserted result.

join_cases.query: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id ORDER BY orders.id ASC
join_cases.note: issue #1544: INNER JOIN ON, base-table-first condition order; order id=4 (customer_id=99) has no matching customer and is dropped

join_cases.query: SELECT * FROM orders LEFT JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id ORDER BY orders.id ASC
join_cases.note: issue #1544: LEFT JOIN keeps the unmatched left row (id=4) with NULL joined columns. Written base-table-first (orders.customer_id = customers.id); the reversed order is exercised by J005 (issue #1555)

join_cases.query: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id WHERE customers.name = 'Alice' ORDER BY orders.id ASC
join_cases.note: issue #1544: JOIN combined with a WHERE predicate on a joined-table column

join_cases.query: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id ORDER BY orders.id ASC
join_cases.note: issue #1555: identical to J001 but with the ON condition written joined-table-first — both engines must orient the condition by which side names the joined table (was documented_divergences D002)

join_cases.query: SELECT * FROM orders_u JOIN customers_u USING (id) ORDER BY orders_u.id ASC
join_cases.note: issue #1544: JOIN USING (single column); both engines resolve USING(id) against each row's primary id, order_u id=99 has no matching customer and is dropped

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: issue #1544: GROUP BY with COUNT(*), executed via Database::execute_aggregate (core) / the default WASM SELECT pipeline. Uses an explicit AS alias; G010 covers the default names

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: issue #1544: GROUP BY + HAVING filters out groups that don't satisfy the aggregate predicate

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, SUM(year) AS total_year FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: issue #1544: SUM aggregate per group

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(year) AS total_year FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY n DESC, category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: issue #1544: multiple aggregates per group and ORDER BY an aggregate column plus the group key. LIMIT on grouped rows is exercised by G005

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(year) AS total_year FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY n DESC, category ASC LIMIT 1
aggregate_cases.note: issue #1556: LIMIT applies to the ordered group rows in both engines (was documented_divergences D006 — core returned every group)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY COUNT(*) ASC, category DESC LIMIT 1
aggregate_cases.note: ORDER BY repeats an aggregate the SELECT stores under an alias: both engines sort by the aliased column. Both used to look the row up under the aggregate's default name, compare every group as equal and fall through to the tie-breaker, which alone puts tech first

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, AVG(year) AS mean_year FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY AVG(year) ASC, category DESC
aggregate_cases.note: same as G006 for AVG

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(year) > 5000 ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: HAVING tests an aggregate the SELECT does not list. Core used to accumulate only the SELECT's aggregates, read SUM(year) as absent and drop every group; WASM computed it

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS year FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY year DESC
aggregate_cases.note: ORDER BY `year` names the count, the aggregate aliased `year`; the payload field `year` is not a column of the grouped rows

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*), SUM(year), AVG(year) FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY count DESC
aggregate_cases.note: unaliased aggregates carry the same default names in both engines (AggregateFunction::result_key), and ORDER BY can name them. WASM used to output count(*), sum(year) and avg(year) (formerly documented_divergences D001)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(category) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: COUNT(column) counts the non-null values of any type; core counted numeric values only and returned 0 for a string column

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: a grouped row carries its GROUP BY columns and aggregates only; WASM used to add a selected column outside GROUP BY from the group's first row

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY id ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 2
aggregate_cases.note: a GROUP BY column resolves as in WHERE: `id` is the point id (core read a payload field `id` and put every row in one NULL group)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 GROUP BY grp ORDER BY grp ASC
aggregate_cases.note: ORDER BY puts NULL last in ASC (core sorted it first)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 GROUP BY grp ORDER BY grp DESC
aggregate_cases.note: and first in DESC (core sorted it last)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, FIRST(year) AS y FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: outside a vector GROUP BY, FIRST reads the group's row with the smallest point id (other: id 3, tech: id 1), whatever order the engine scans in

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, AVG(year) AS score FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY category ASC
aggregate_cases.note: a SQL GROUP BY may name an aggregate `score` or `id`; only a vector GROUP BY, whose groups carry their own, refuses it (V017)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 GROUP BY grp ORDER BY n DESC
aggregate_cases.note: groups equal on every ORDER BY key fall back to their GROUP BY key, ascending (y before NULL)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY year
aggregate_cases.note: without ORDER BY, SQL GROUP BY groups come by GROUP BY key ascending (core returned hash order, WASM scan order)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) = 2 OR COUNT(*) > 0 AND COUNT(*) > 5
aggregate_cases.note: HAVING AND binds tighter than OR, as in SQL: n = 2 OR (n > 0 AND n > 5). Read left to right, the condition kept no group

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT kind, COUNT(id) AS n, MAX(id) AS top FROM tickets WHERE id >= 32 GROUP BY kind
aggregate_cases.note: the WHERE of an aggregate reads `id` as the point id, as its aggregates do, although every payload carries an `id` of its own

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT x, COUNT(*) AS n FROM nums WHERE id <= 4 GROUP BY x
aggregate_cases.note: `-0.0` and `0` are one group, `1.0` and `1` another, each keyed by its integer

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT x, MIN(x) AS low, MAX(x) AS top FROM nums WHERE id <= 4 GROUP BY x
aggregate_cases.note: MIN and MAX of values equal by value return the integer, whichever row comes first (`-0.0` and `1.0` come first here)

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT x, MAX(x) AS top FROM nums GROUP BY x HAVING MAX(x) > 9007199254740992.0
aggregate_cases.note: HAVING compares an integer aggregate with a float threshold exactly, as WHERE does: 2^53 + 1 is greater than the float 2^53

aggregate_cases.query: SELECT x, COUNT(*) AS n FROM nums GROUP BY x HAVING MAX(x) = 0.3

setops_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC UNION SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'other' ORDER BY year ASC
setops_cases.note: issue #1544: UNION of two disjoint partitions returns every id exactly once. Compared as a SET, not an ordered list — see documented_divergences D003

setops_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC UNION SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
setops_cases.note: issue #1544: UNION of a branch with itself proves de-duplication (3 ids, not 6). Compared as a SET — see documented_divergences D003

setops_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE year >= 2020 ORDER BY year ASC INTERSECT SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
setops_cases.note: issue #1544: INTERSECT keeps only ids present in both branches. Compared as a SET — see documented_divergences D003

setops_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC EXCEPT SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'other' ORDER BY year ASC
setops_cases.note: issue #1544: EXCEPT removes the right-hand branch's ids from the left-hand branch. Compared as a SET — see documented_divergences D003

match_cases.core_query: SELECT * FROM people WHERE MATCH (a:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person) ORDER BY people.id ASC
match_cases.wasm_query: MATCH (a:Person@people)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person@people) RETURN a ORDER BY a.id ASC
match_cases.note: issue #1544: 1-hop MATCH. Query text differs per engine by design — see documented_divergences D004: core treats vector-collection points as graph nodes (SELECT ... WHERE MATCH over the 'people' vector collection); WASM keeps a separate in-memory graph store addressed via @collection annotations and the standalone MATCH ... RETURN form. Both graphs encode the SAME topology (chain 1->2->3->4, label KNOWS) and are asserted against the SAME golden ids

match_cases.core_query: SELECT * FROM people WHERE MATCH (a:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(c:Person) ORDER BY people.id ASC
match_cases.wasm_query: MATCH (a:Person@people)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person@people)-[:KNOWS]->(c:Person@people) RETURN a ORDER BY a.id ASC
match_cases.note: issue #1544: 2-hop MATCH over the same chain topology as M001

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: NEAR ranks every point by cosine similarity to $a; $a was chosen so no two points tie

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a LIMIT 2
near_cases.note: NEAR + LIMIT keeps the k best

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
near_cases.note: OFFSET on a ranked result skips the best hit

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND category = 'tech' LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: hybrid NEAR + metadata: the predicate is a hard filter and the vector ranking is kept

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND (category = 'other' OR year = 2020) LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: hybrid NEAR + a parenthesized OR filter

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a ORDER BY similarity() ASC LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: ORDER BY similarity() ASC reverses the natural ranking

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a ORDER BY year ASC LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: ORDER BY a payload column re-orders the NEAR hits and keeps each hit's similarity score

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND similarity(vector, $a) > 0.5 LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: NEAR + similarity() threshold on the same vector

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE similarity(vector, $a) > 0.35 LIMIT 5
near_cases.note: similarity() threshold without NEAR: rows are ranked by that similarity and carry it as their score (was documented_divergences D011)

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE similarity(vector, $a) > 0.35 ORDER BY year ASC
near_cases.note: similarity() threshold + ORDER BY a column: the column decides the order, the score is still the similarity

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE similarity(vector, $a) > 0.35 AND category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
near_cases.note: similarity() threshold combined with a metadata predicate

near_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE similarity(vector, $a) <= 0.35 ORDER BY year ASC

fusion_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] LIMIT 5
fusion_cases.note: NEAR_FUSED without a strategy fuses the two per-vector rankings with RRF (k=60)

fusion_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'average' LIMIT 5
fusion_cases.note: average fusion; $a and $b were chosen so rrf, average and maximum give three different orders

fusion_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'maximum' LIMIT 5
SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'rrf' (k=1) LIMIT 5
fusion_cases.note: an explicit RRF k reaches the fused scores

fusion_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'maximum' AND category = 'tech' LIMIT 5
fusion_cases.note: NEAR_FUSED + metadata: the predicate filters before fusion

fusion_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] LIMIT 5 USING FUSION (strategy = 'rrf')
fusion_cases.note: a trailing USING FUSION clause over a NEAR_FUSED is valid

rejected_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'weighted' LIMIT 5
rejected_cases.note: NEAR_FUSED accepts only rrf, average or maximum: weighted is ill-defined over homogeneous query vectors (V012). Was documented_divergences D010

rejected_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR_FUSED [$a, $b] USING FUSION 'rsf' LIMIT 5
rejected_cases.note: NEAR_FUSED refuses rsf for the same reason (V012). Was documented_divergences D010

rejected_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND category = 'tech' LIMIT 5 USING FUSION (strategy = 'rrf')
rejected_cases.note: USING FUSION needs two fusable branches; a single NEAR plus a metadata filter has one (V012). Was documented_divergences D010

rejected_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND category = 'tech' LIMIT 5 USING FUSION (strategy = 'weighted')
rejected_cases.note: same as R003 for a weight-sensitive strategy

rejected_cases.query: MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN d.year ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3
rejected_cases.note: a MATCH ORDER BY aggregate has no GROUP BY to rank (V015, refused at validation by both engines)

rejected_cases.query: MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN d.year ORDER BY MAX(year) LIMIT 3
rejected_cases.note: same as R005 for an aggregate over a property (V015)

rejected_cases.query: MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN d.year ORDER BY d LIMIT 3
rejected_cases.note: a bare pattern alias names a node, not a sortable value (V015)

rejected_cases.query: MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN d.year AS y ORDER BY y LIMIT 3
rejected_cases.note: a RETURN alias is not a property path MATCH can sort by (V015)

rejected_cases.query: MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN d.year ORDER BY year LIMIT 3
rejected_cases.note: an unqualified property is not a property path MATCH can sort by; qualify it as d.year (V015)

rejected_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category ORDER BY SUM(year) DESC
rejected_cases.note: ORDER BY an aggregate the SELECT does not list names no column of the grouped rows (V016); both engines used to accept it and return the groups unsorted

rejected_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM docs GROUP BY category, count
rejected_cases.note: the GROUP BY column `count` and COUNT(*)'s default name share an output field; core used to keep the count and drop the column without a word

rejected_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(year) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category
rejected_cases.note: two aggregates aliased alike share an output field; one used to overwrite the other

rejected_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS score FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category
rejected_cases.note: in a vector GROUP BY an aggregate named `score` (or `id`) would shadow the group's own score (id) when sorting

rejected_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 'many'
rejected_cases.note: a HAVING threshold must be a number: every group used to fail the comparison silently

rejected_cases.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
rejected_cases.note: HAVING requires GROUP BY in both engines (WASM filtered the single implicit group)

statements: UPDATE docs SET category = 'archived' WHERE year < 2021
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'archived' ORDER BY year ASC
dml_cases.note: UPDATE with a range predicate; the new value is visible to an equality filter

statements: UPDATE docs SET year = 2030 WHERE category = 'other'
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year DESC
dml_cases.note: UPDATE of a sort key; the two updated rows tie on 2030 and fall back to ascending id

statements: UPDATE docs SET category = 'x' WHERE id = 99
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
dml_cases.note: UPDATE matching no row changes nothing

statements: UPDATE docs SET rank = 1 WHERE category LIKE 'te%'
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY year ASC
dml_cases.note: UPDATE adds a field that did not exist, selected by LIKE

statements: UPDATE docs SET category = 'tech' WHERE year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021 AND category = 'other'
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE category = 'tech' ORDER BY year ASC
dml_cases.note: UPDATE with a conjunctive BETWEEN predicate

statements: UPDATE docs SET category = 'other' WHERE id = 4
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a AND category = 'other' LIMIT 5
dml_cases.note: a payload UPDATE is visible to a filtered NEAR and leaves the vector untouched

statements: DELETE FROM docs WHERE id IN (2, 5)
dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs ORDER BY year ASC
dml_cases.note: DELETE by id list. Only id predicates are common to both engines — see documented_divergences D007

dml_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a LIMIT 5
dml_cases.note: a deleted point no longer ranks in NEAR

projection_cases.query: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM docs ORDER BY category ASC
projection_cases.note: DISTINCT then ORDER BY on the distinct column (was documented_divergences D012)

projection_cases.query: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM docs ORDER BY category ASC LIMIT 1
projection_cases.note: LIMIT applies to the ordered distinct rows

projection_cases.query: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM docs WHERE year >= 2022 ORDER BY category ASC
SELECT DISTINCT category FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a LIMIT 5
projection_cases.note: DISTINCT keeps the first row of each value in ranking order: id 4 (tech) ranks before id 3 (other)

projection_cases.query: SELECT category, year FROM docs WHERE category LIKE 'o%' ORDER BY year DESC
projection_cases.note: named-column projection keeps only the selected fields

projection_cases.query: SELECT DISTINCT id FROM nums WHERE id <= 4 ORDER BY id
projection_cases.note: DISTINCT `id` keys on the point id, although each payload carries the same `id` of its own

projection_cases.query: SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY x ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM nums WHERE id <= 4 ORDER BY id
projection_cases.note: PARTITION BY keys numbers as GROUP BY does: `-0.0` with `0`, `1.0` with `1`

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT category, MAX(score) AS best FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category ORDER BY similarity() DESC
vector_group_cases.note: vector GROUP BY (NEAR + GROUP BY) orders groups by their score, the best row's: tech 0.730 (id 4), other 0.548 (id 3)

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT category, MAX(score) AS best FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category ORDER BY similarity() ASC
vector_group_cases.note: same as V001 ascending, which first-seen ranking order alone does not give

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT category, MAX(score) AS best FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category ORDER BY MAX(score) ASC
vector_group_cases.note: an ORDER BY aggregate of a vector GROUP BY sorts on the SELECT item it repeats

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(year) AS total, AVG(year) AS mean, MIN(year) AS lo, MAX(year) AS hi, FIRST(year) AS top FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category ORDER BY COUNT(*) ASC
vector_group_cases.note: every aggregate is computed per group (core returned null for all but MAX/AVG(score) and FIRST), FIRST reads the best row, and each group is its best row's id with the group score

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 2
vector_group_cases.note: HAVING filters vector GROUP BY groups (core ignored it)

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs WHERE vector NEAR $a GROUP BY year
vector_group_cases.note: without ORDER BY, groups come best score first, ties by best-row id (core returned hash order)

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 WHERE vector NEAR $e GROUP BY grp ORDER BY similarity() DESC
vector_group_cases.note: Euclidean: similarity() DESC puts the nearest group first (WASM sorted raw distances). A row without the group column forms the NULL group, as in SQL GROUP BY (core dropped it)

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 WHERE vector NEAR $e GROUP BY grp
vector_group_cases.note: Euclidean default order: nearest group first, each group's best row being its nearest

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 WHERE vector NEAR $e GROUP BY grp ORDER BY grp ASC
vector_group_cases.note: the NULL group sorts last in ASC, as in every ORDER BY

vector_group_cases.query: SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS n FROM docs_l2 WHERE vector NEAR $e GROUP BY grp ORDER BY grp DESC

null_order_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs_l2 ORDER BY grp ASC
null_order_cases.note: a missing or null ORDER BY key sorts after every value in ASC (core sorted it first); ties keep ascending id

null_order_cases.query: SELECT * FROM docs_l2 ORDER BY grp DESC
null_order_cases.note: and before every value in DESC (core sorted it last)

null_order_cases.query: SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE id > 31 ORDER BY id DESC
null_order_cases.note: `id` is the point id in WHERE and ORDER BY, as in projection, GROUP BY and aggregates, although each payload carries an `id` of its own (3, 1, 2); core read the payload field and returned no row

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = -0.0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x <= 0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x > 0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x >= 0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: an integer literal equals the float of the same value

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 1.0 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: and a float literal the integer

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 0.3 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 0.30000000000000004 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x BETWEEN 0.29999 AND 0.30001 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: a range gives the tolerance an equality no longer has

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x != 1 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: `!=` is the complement of `=`, every path included

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x NOT IN (0, 1) ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x IN (0.3, 1, 3.5) ORDER BY id

number_cases.note: the same past 16 values, where IN switches to a binary search

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x IN (-0.00000000000000001, 0) ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x > 9007199254740992.0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x = 9007199254740992.0 ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x < 0.00000000000000002 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: an ordering on a float that tiny is exact too

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums ORDER BY x ASC LIMIT 5
number_cases.note: ORDER BY ties `-0.0` with `0` (ascending id) and orders every number exactly

number_cases.query: SELECT * FROM nums ORDER BY x DESC LIMIT 2
SELECT * FROM nums WHERE x != 0.00000000000000001 ORDER BY id
number_cases.note: `0` and `-0.0` differ from `0.00000000000000001`, every path included

documented_divergences.core_behavior: normalize_join_condition (search/query/join.rs) accepts ON in either order — `base.col = joined.col` and `joined.col = base.col` both resolve to the same match
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: RESOLVED (issue #1555): equality_keys (velesql_join.rs) now orients the condition by which side targets the join alias (or raw table name), mirroring core; both orders resolve identically
documented_divergences.status: resolved by issue #1555 — join case J005 exercises the joined-table-first order on both engines; the former regression-lock canary test is now a parity lock (test_wasm_join_condition_side_order_parity_1555)

documented_divergences.area: UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT row ordering for non-ranked branches
documented_divergences.core_behavior: apply_set_operation (set_operations.rs) always re-sorts the merged result by score descending, regardless of any per-branch ORDER BY; when every row has score 0.0 (no vector NEAR in either branch) the comparator sees only ties and Vec::sort_unstable_by's tie-break is not stable — order was observed to differ between two consecutive runs of the SAME core binary for the identical query
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: velesql_setops.rs concatenates branches left-to-right and de-duplicates first-seen, so each branch's own ORDER BY is preserved in the final row sequence — deterministic, but not the same sequence as core's
documented_divergences.status: accepted — neither behaviour is wrong (SQL does not guarantee an order for UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT without an explicit outer ORDER BY, which this query engine does not yet apply to compound results). fixture setops_cases S001-S004 assert result MEMBERSHIP and COUNT only (ids compared as a sorted set), never exact order

documented_divergences.area: MATCH data model (core unified vs WASM separate graph store)
documented_divergences.core_behavior: graph nodes ARE vector-collection points (payload `_labels` field); edges live on the same Collection via add_edge; MATCH is expressed as `SELECT ... FROM <collection> WHERE MATCH (...)`
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: graph nodes/edges live in a separate in-memory graph store per name, populated via `INSERT NODE`/`INSERT EDGE`, addressed from pattern nodes via `@collection` annotations, and queried with the standalone `MATCH ... RETURN` form — there is no requirement for a same-named vector collection to exist
documented_divergences.status: accepted architectural difference (WASM has no persistence layer to unify with); fixture match_cases M001/M002 carry a `core_query`/`wasm_query` pair instead of one shared query string, both encoding the same graph topology, asserted against the same golden ids

documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: WASM-local relative_score/rsf multi-query fusion ranks differently from core
documented_divergences.status: pre-existing, out of scope for issue #1544 — cross-referenced here only because the issue's own description flagged it as related context

documented_divergences.area: LIMIT on GROUP BY aggregate results
documented_divergences.core_behavior: RESOLVED (issue #1556): build_grouped_results now applies OFFSET/LIMIT after ORDER BY, with no default cap — a LIMIT-less GROUP BY still returns every group
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: the WASM aggregate pipeline applies LIMIT to the grouped row set the same as a plain SELECT; both engines now agree
documented_divergences.status: resolved by issue #1556 — aggregate case G005 exercises LIMIT on grouped rows and is asserted by both engines; unit coverage in crates/velesdb-core/tests/velesql_group_by_limit.rs
documented_divergences.evidence: crates/velesdb-core/src/collection/search/query/aggregation/grouped.rs: build_grouped_results applies skip(offset)/take(limit) after sort; crates/velesdb-wasm/src/velesql_select.rs: finalize_aggregated routes through apply_limit_offset with u64::MAX default

documented_divergences.core_behavior: DELETE accepts only `id = N` or `id IN (N1, N2, ...)`; any other WHERE is refused with "DELETE WHERE must use 'id = N' or 'id IN (N1, N2, ...)'"
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: DELETE evaluates any WHERE predicate row by row and removes every match (e.g. `DELETE FROM docs WHERE category = 'other'`)
documented_divergences.status: accepted — WASM is a superset: every DELETE core accepts gives the same rows on both engines (dml_cases W007/W008), and the extra WASM shapes are refused by core rather than answered differently. Narrowing the browser engine would break callers for no correctness gain

documented_divergences.core_behavior: UPDATE may assign the `vector` column on a vector collection (apply_assignments_to_point re-parses it as the new embedding)
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: UPDATE refuses `SET vector = ...` with "UPDATE cannot modify the 'vector' column (use UPSERT)"; payload assignments behave as in core
documented_divergences.status: accepted — WASM is a subset here; the fixture's dml_cases assign payload fields only. UPSERT is the WASM way to replace an embedding

documented_divergences.area: score of rows that no vector ranked
documented_divergences.core_behavior: a scan with no NEAR, NEAR_FUSED or similarity() predicate returns every row with score 1.0
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: the same rows carry score 0.0 (QueryResultRow::score in the JavaScript API)
documented_divergences.status: accepted — the value carries no ranking on either engine and SELECT * does not project it; only the vector cases (near_cases, fusion_cases, and the dml_cases that end in a NEAR) assert scores
documented_divergences.evidence: scalar-only cases (X001-X020) on both engines; crates/velesdb-wasm/src/velesql_select.rs: execute_plain()

documented_divergences.area: USING FUSION validation (single-branch NEAR, NEAR_FUSED weighted/rsf)
documented_divergences.core_behavior: QueryValidator refuses USING FUSION over a single NEAR (nothing to fuse) and NEAR_FUSED with weighted or rsf (V012)
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: RESOLVED: the WASM executor now runs core's QueryValidator::validate before dispatch. It used to accept a single NEAR with USING FUSION rrf/maximum/average and re-rank it against a constant metadata branch (for rrf the order changed and the scores became RRF scores), and to run NEAR_FUSED weighted/rsf as rrf
documented_divergences.status: resolved — rejected_cases R001-R004 require both engines to refuse

documented_divergences.core_behavior: the rows that pass the threshold are ranked by that similarity and carry it as their score
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: RESOLVED: the plain scan now scores each row with the similarity it was filtered on and ranks by it in the metric's direction. It used to return the rows in insertion order with score 0.0, so ORDER BY similarity() had nothing to sort on
documented_divergences.status: resolved — near_cases N009-N012 assert ids and scores on both engines

documented_divergences.core_behavior: DISTINCT runs first (apply_distinct), then ORDER BY, OFFSET and LIMIT (default 10)
documented_divergences.wasm_behavior: RESOLVED: a DISTINCT without aggregates now goes through the plain SELECT pipeline and core's apply_distinct. It used to run in the aggregation pipeline, which ignored ORDER BY, had no default LIMIT, and keyed `DISTINCT *` on id and score so no row ever collapsed
documented_divergences.status: resolved — projection_cases P001-P004 assert the projected rows on both engines
